item.title: Match phrasing style across parallel doc examples
item.description: When clarifying one example in a docs section, reviewers expect the same phrasing pattern applied to sibling examples.
item.content: If you rewrite one tip as 'Accessing the URL with a trailing slash (``/about/``)', apply the identical construction to the parallel tip (e.g. 'If you access the URL without a trailing slash (``/projects``)'). Inconsistent placement of the URL literal across adjacent examples gets flagged.

item.title: Inline concrete URL examples next to abstract descriptions
item.description: Adding the literal URL in parentheses beside 'with/without a trailing slash' makes docs clearer for non-native readers.
item.content: When docs say 'with a trailing slash' or 'without a trailing slash', append the concrete path like (``/projects``) or (``/about/``) so readers can see exactly what is meant. This was the accepted change.

item.title: Keep doc edits minimal and reflow only touched lines
item.description: Small clarification PRs should change only the sentences in question and rewrap them cleanly.
item.content: For tiny docs clarifications, avoid restructuring surrounding text; edit the specific sentences, keep line lengths consistent with the file, and let the diff stay small so review focuses on wording.

item.title: Avoid introducing new grammar errors in doc fixes
item.description: The first attempt replaced 'white and blacklisting' with 'allows controlling with file extensions', which reviewers flagged as a likely 'with'/'which' typo.
item.content: When rewording documentation, proofread the new sentence for grammar before submitting. If a reviewer asks whether a word was meant to be another, that signals a typo you introduced, not a stylistic preference.

item.title: Replace outdated terminology like whitelist/blacklist
item.description: The accepted fix removed 'white and blacklisting' in favor of neutral wording about controlling which extensions are allowed.
item.content: In doc updates, prefer inclusive phrasing such as 'allows controlling which extensions are allowed' over whitelist/blacklist terms, and make sure the replacement sentence reads cleanly.

item.title: Expand terse parameter docs with explicit behavior
item.description: The accepted change clarified category_filter by stating only listed categories are returned, rather than just calling it a whitelist.
item.content: For docstring params, describe the actual effect ('Only categories in the list will be returned') instead of relying on a single loaded term, so readers understand behavior without extra context.

item.title: Use super() for base class initialization
item.description: When refactoring to introduce a shared base class, reviewers expect super() calls rather than explicit base class name calls.
item.content: Replace explicit `BaseClass.__init__(self, ...)` calls with `super().__init__(...)` when moving to a new base class. This is a common review requirement and avoids hardcoding the parent class name.

item.title: Remove leftover commented code before submitting
item.description: Reviewers reject diffs that contain commented-out code left over from refactoring.
item.content: After moving or deleting code, delete the old blocks entirely rather than commenting them out. Leftover commented code is flagged in review and signals an unfinished change.

item.title: Extract shared base class for common API
item.description: When two classes need a common API, create a shared base class and move shared attributes/methods into it, updating both to inherit.
item.content: For issues like 'Common API Between X and Y', introduce a base class (e.g. Scaffold) holding shared attributes and setup methods, have both classes inherit from it, and move helper functions/constants (like setupmethod, _sentinel, _endpoint_from_view_func) into the new module. Update imports and CHANGES.rst accordingly.

item.title: Follow pre-commit's documented cache key recipe exactly
item.description: The pre-commit docs prescribe a specific cache key pattern using a hashed full Python version, and deviating from it gets rejected.
item.content: Use the exact snippet from https://pre-commit.com/#github-actions-example: set PY via `python -VV | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1` and key the cache as `pre-commit|${{ env.PY }}|${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}`. Reviewers expect the documented form, not a hand-rolled variant.

item.title: Read linked docs before implementing a fix
item.description: The issue linked the authoritative pre-commit docs and comment; the first attempt ignored the exact command they specify.
item.content: When an issue cites documentation URLs, open them and mirror the referenced example verbatim (commands, env var names, key format). The reviewer's rejection cited the same docs, so matching them upfront avoids a round trip.

item.title: Use full Python version in cache keys, not matrix shorthand
item.description: Caching on `matrix.python` (e.g. '3.8') is too coarse; pre-commit needs the full version to avoid stale caches.
item.content: Derive a stable full-version token (e.g. hash of `python -VV`) and use it in the cache key instead of the matrix Python label. This prevents cache collisions across patch releases, as recommended in pre-commit issue #1575.

item.title: Break reference cycles with weakref lambdas
item.description: When a constructor stores a bound method that references self, it creates a cycle preventing refcount-based cleanup.
item.content: Replace bound-method references stored on the instance with a lambda capturing a weakref.ref(self), then call self_ref().method(**kw). This breaks the cycle so CPython frees the object when external refs drop.

item.title: Add weakref-based GC tests for cycle fixes
item.description: Reviewers asked for test coverage proving the reference cycle is actually broken.
item.content: Write a test that disables gc, creates the object, takes a weakref.ref, deletes the object, and asserts the weakref is now None. Gate it with a skipif on CPython since it relies on refcount semantics.

item.title: Anticipate reviewer requests for tests
item.description: The first attempt was rejected partly for lacking test coverage of the fix.
item.content: When fixing a subtle lifecycle/GC issue, proactively include a focused regression test demonstrating the behavior change, rather than waiting for reviewers to request it.

item.title: Split parametrize into separate named parameters
item.description: When converting a loop over tuples into pytest parametrize, use distinct parameter names rather than a single combined name.
item.content: Reviewers reject `@pytest.mark.parametrize("passing", ...)` style where each case is one opaque tuple. Instead use `@pytest.mark.parametrize("args, expected", (...))` so each tuple element maps to a named test argument and failures are readable.

item.title: Convert loop bodies directly into parametrized test bodies
item.description: Move the loop's assertions into the test function body and pass the loop variables as parameters.
item.content: For `for args, expected in passing: assert f(*args) == expected`, the parametrized test becomes `def test_x(self, args, expected): assert f(*args) == expected`. Keep the original comment describing the case group above the parametrize decorator.

item.title: Parametrize exception tests with only the input parameter
item.description: For loops that only check raised exceptions, parametrize just the input and keep the pytest.raises block in the body.
item.content: When the loop is `for args in failing: with pytest.raises(NotFound): ...`, use `@pytest.mark.parametrize("args", (...))` and `def test_x(self, args): with pytest.raises(NotFound): ...`. Don't invent an expected-exception parameter unless cases differ.

item.title: Use ordered literals for deterministic iteration
item.description: When iterating over a fixed set of candidate names where order affects which one wins, use a tuple/list, not a set.
item.content: Sets have no guaranteed iteration order, so code that picks the first matching candidate from a set is non-deterministic. Replace set literals with tuples when the order of preference matters.

item.title: Make minimal targeted fixes for reported bugs
item.description: When an issue describes a specific defect (non-deterministic set iteration), fix exactly that rather than adding extra logic.
item.content: The reviewer rejected an attempt that added extra behavior alongside the fix. Keep the change scoped to what the issue asks for; avoid introducing parallel logic paths that weren't requested.

item.title: Prefer single source of truth over duplicate logic
item.description: Reviewers dislike having two code paths doing similar things with different logic; consolidate instead.
item.content: If you find yourself implementing the same concept twice (e.g., two factory-discovery branches with divergent logic), refactor to one path. Duplicated logic with subtle differences is a common rejection reason.

item.title: Test through public API, not internals
item.description: Reviewers rejected calling JSONEncoder().encode directly; use json.dumps instead.
item.content: When testing serialization behavior, exercise the public entry point (e.g. flask.json.dumps) rather than instantiating the encoder class directly, since that reflects the typical use case and is what reviewers expect.

item.title: Keep test additions minimal and scoped
item.description: First attempt added redundant asserts, unnecessary classes, and deleted an unrelated test file.
item.content: Add only the test needed for the new behavior. Avoid extra asserts, helper classes, or class attributes when a plain string or module-level function suffices, and never delete or rewrite existing test files that cover other behavior.

item.title: Preserve existing tests when adding new ones
item.description: Removing tests/test_helpers.py content was flagged as a serious mistake.
item.content: When adding a test, append to the appropriate existing file without removing unrelated tests or helpers; deleting coverage of other behavior will get the change rejected even if the new test is correct.

item.title: Simplify README examples for first-time users
item.description: When updating docs examples, prioritize the simplest cross-platform path over showing configuration details.
item.content: For introductory README examples, avoid env-var prefixes like `env FLASK_APP=...` that break on Windows and add incidental complexity. Use the default filename (e.g. app.py) so the command is just `flask run`, and point readers to full docs for discovery details.

item.title: Make required file naming explicit in examples
item.description: Reviewers asked for an explicit comment stating the filename the example must be saved as.
item.content: When an example relies on a conventional filename for tooling to work, add a comment like `# save this as app.py` so users don't silently break the command. Anticipate reviewer requests for explicitness.

item.title: Align example output with actual command output
item.description: Keep sample terminal output consistent with the simplified command shown.
item.content: When trimming commands in docs, also trim the sample output to match what the new command actually prints, and keep prompt markers (e.g. `$`) consistent across code blocks.

item.title: Replace OrderedDict with plain dict when order is guaranteed
item.description: Modern Python (3.7+) guarantees dict insertion order, so OrderedDict is unnecessary for order-sensitive internal APIs.
item.content: When refactoring, don't preserve OrderedDict just to signal that order matters. Use a plain dict and document the ordering guarantee in the docstring instead, since dicts are ordered in all supported Pythons.

item.title: Replace all setdefault calls, not just the first
item.description: When converting dicts to defaultdicts, reviewers expect every setdefault/get-with-default pattern to be simplified consistently.
item.content: After making a dict a defaultdict, sweep the whole codebase for every `.setdefault(key, default)` and `.get(key, default)` on that dict and replace them with direct indexing. Missing even one leaves the refactor incomplete and triggers review comments.

item.title: Use nested defaultdict factories for two-level maps
item.description: A dict-of-dict-of-dict can be replaced with `defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(dict))` to eliminate chained setdefault calls.
item.content: For multi-level lookup structures like error_handler_spec, construct them as `defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(dict))` so lookups like `spec[name][code]` auto-create intermediate levels, removing the need for `.setdefault(name, {}).get(c)`.

item.title: Follow reviewer guidance on module placement
item.description: When a reviewer rejects reintroducing a removed module, implement the suggested inline approach instead.
item.content: If a reviewer says not to bring back a deleted module (e.g. `_compat`), place the compatibility shim directly in the file they indicate (e.g. after imports in `app.py`) rather than creating a new module. Honor the exact location and structure they propose.

item.title: Version-gate stdlib bug workarounds
item.description: Guard compatibility shims for fixed stdlib bugs behind a version check so newer Pythons use the native function.
item.content: For bugs fixed in a later Python version (like bpo-33261 fixed in 3.8), define the workaround only under `if sys.version_info < (3, 8):` and otherwise alias the stdlib function directly. This avoids unnecessary overhead and keeps behavior aligned with upstream.

item.title: Unwrap partials and methods before coroutine check
item.description: To detect wrapped coroutine functions, unwrap `functools.partial` and bound methods before calling `inspect.iscoroutinefunction`.
item.content: Loop `while inspect.ismethod(func): func = func.__func__` and `while isinstance(func, functools.partial): func = func.func`, then call `inspect.iscoroutinefunction(func)`. This handles partially-wrapped coroutines that the stdlib check misses on older Pythons.

item.title: Verify cancellation semantics before documenting them
item.description: The reviewer questioned whether spawned tasks are cancelled or merely stopped, requiring a source-code citation to confirm.
item.content: When documenting lifecycle behavior of async tasks or event loops, verify the exact semantics (cancelled vs. stopped vs. abandoned) against the underlying library source before writing. Cite the specific implementation (e.g., asgiref's sync.py) so reviewers can confirm.

item.title: Name concrete APIs in documentation examples
item.description: The reviewer suggested explicitly naming ``asyncio.create_task`` rather than vaguely describing spawning tasks.
item.content: In docs explaining what users cannot do, name the specific API or function (e.g., ``asyncio.create_task``) so readers can map the guidance to their code. Vague phrasing like 'spawn tasks' invites review suggestions to be concrete.

item.title: Pair limitations with a working alternative
item.description: The accepted docs explained the background-task limitation and then pointed to the ASGI adapter as the supported workaround.
item.content: When documenting a limitation, immediately follow it with the recommended alternative (task queue, or ASGI server with WsgiToAsgi adapter) and cross-reference the relevant section. This turns a negative note into actionable guidance and satisfies reviewers.

item.title: Relaxing a dependency version constraint
item.description: When loosening a minimum version requirement, also add a runtime deprecation warning and document the future hard requirement.
item.content: Lower the pin in setup.py (e.g. click>=7.1.2), emit a DeprecationWarning at runtime when the old version is detected, and update CHANGES.rst to explain the temporary compatibility window and when the hard dependency returns.

item.title: Keep default tox env working when adding variant envs
item.description: Adding a special-case tox env (like click7) must not break the default `tox -e py` run.
item.content: Use conditional deps syntax (`!click7: ...` / `click7: ...`) so the default env still installs the normal dependency, and only add the variant to envlist without tagging the main env. Reviewers flagged removing a click8 tag that broke `tox -e py`.

item.title: Test version-conditional deprecation warnings
item.description: Write tests that branch on the installed dependency version so they pass under both old and new versions.
item.content: Patch the CLI entry point, then use `pytest.deprecated_call` when the old version is installed and call normally otherwise. This keeps CI green across the version matrix while still asserting the warning fires.

item.title: Match project documentation formatting conventions
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it used only one blank line above a section header, while the project keeps two empty lines above headers.
item.content: Before editing docs, inspect surrounding headers and blank-line spacing to infer the project's RST style. In Flask docs, keep two empty lines above section headers; reviewers enforce this.

item.title: Use admonitions for version-specific platform tips
item.description: Adding a Windows/Python 3.8 async caveat as an RST admonition with a clear error message and upgrade advice was accepted.
item.content: When documenting known bugs tied to a specific Python version or platform, use an admonition block, quote the exact error text users will see, and state the concrete remedy (e.g., upgrade to Python 3.9).

item.title: Keep doc tips concise and actionable
item.description: The accepted change was a short admonition naming the error and the fix, without extra links or workarounds.
item.content: For issue-driven doc additions, prefer a minimal tip that identifies the symptom and the recommended action; avoid speculative workarounds or external links unless the issue explicitly asks for them.

item.title: Parameterize the customization point, not the wrapper
item.description: Reviewers preferred exposing a small overridable `async_to_sync` hook over making users reimplement the whole `ensure_sync` boilerplate.
item.content: When adding an extension point, isolate the minimal behavior users actually need to customize (e.g., the coroutine-to-sync conversion) into its own overridable method, and have the broader method delegate to it. This avoids forcing users to duplicate boilerplate like `iscoroutinefunction` checks.

item.title: Apply ensure_sync at call sites, not registration
item.description: Wrapping callbacks at registration time breaks identity checks and requires unwrapping hacks; wrapping at invocation is cleaner.
item.content: Store user callbacks as-is and call `self.ensure_sync(func)(...)` at the point of invocation (dispatch, error handlers, before-first-request). This avoids `_flask_sync_wrapper`/`__wrapped__` unwrapping logic in `add_url_rule` and keeps overwrite-detection comparisons correct.

item.title: Verify async support with tests and docs together
item.description: Async changes need tests that fail without the change, plus docs and versionchanged notes for extension authors.
item.content: For async-related Flask changes, add tests exercising async views/error handlers, document the extension-author pattern (e.g., calling `current_app.ensure_sync(func)` in decorators) in docs/async-await.rst, and add `.. versionchanged::` entries. Run pre-commit and pytest/tox before submitting.

item.title: Deprecation warning stacklevel must point at caller
item.description: When adding a DeprecationWarning inside a wrapper function, reviewers expect stacklevel=2 so the warning points to the user's calling code, not the wrapper.
item.content: For a deprecation warning emitted directly inside the public function, use stacklevel=2. Only increase it when the warning is emitted from a helper one level deeper than the public API.

item.title: Give deprecated alias parameters a default of None
item.description: Re-adding a removed parameter as a deprecated alias requires a default value so existing calls without it still work.
item.content: Declare the deprecated parameter as `filename: t.Optional[str] = None` and only warn/override when it is not None, preserving backward compatibility without breaking new-style calls.

item.title: Document deprecations in CHANGES and docstrings
item.description: Accepted deprecation changes include a CHANGES.rst entry and a versionchanged directive in the docstring.
item.content: Add a CHANGES.rst bullet noting the re-added parameter and its removal version, plus a `.. versionchanged::` note in the function docstring explaining the rename.

item.title: Combine nested blueprint URL prefixes from both options and blueprint defaults
item.description: When nesting blueprints, the effective url_prefix must consider both the registration option and the blueprint's own url_prefix attribute, and combine them with the parent's prefix.
item.content: Resolve each level's prefix as `options.get('url_prefix') or blueprint.url_prefix` (or explicit None checks) before combining. Only concatenate when both parent and child prefixes are non-None, using `parent.rstrip('/') + '/' + child.lstrip('/')`. This handles the case where url_prefix is passed as None in options.

item.title: Write focused tests that mirror the issue's reproduction snippet
item.description: Reviewers rejected a convoluted test; simpler tests directly demonstrating the reported behavior are preferred.
item.content: When fixing a bug, base the test on the minimal reproduction from the issue report rather than building elaborate multi-level scenarios. Keep assertions direct and easy to verify.

item.title: Copy options dict before mutating during blueprint registration
item.description: Mutating the caller's bp_options dict in place can cause subtle bugs; copy it first.
item.content: In register loops, do `bp_options = bp_options.copy()` before setting keys like url_prefix or name_prefix, so the original registration options aren't mutated across repeated registrations.

item.title: Keep documentation changes out of the changelog
item.description: Reviewers rejected a changelog entry for a docs-only fix because the changelog targets library users, not doc readers.
item.content: When a change only touches documentation (e.g., fixing an example in quickstart.rst), do not add a CHANGES/changelog entry. Changelogs are for user-facing library behavior changes.

item.title: Remove unwanted commits via interactive rebase
item.description: When a reviewer says a commit shouldn't exist, drop it with `git rebase -i` and force-push rather than adding a revert commit.
item.content: If a commit (like an unwanted changelog edit) must be removed, use `git rebase -i` to drop it and force-push the branch. Avoid adding a separate revert commit, which clutters history before squashing.

item.title: Use the imported escape helper in doc examples
item.description: The fix for an unused `escape` import was to actually call `escape()` in the Variable Rules examples of quickstart.rst.
item.content: When docs import a helper like `escape` but never use it, update the example code to wrap user-provided values (e.g., `f'User {escape(username)}'`) so the import is exercised and the example demonstrates safe output.

item.title: Avoid mutating shared blueprint registration state
item.description: When registering nested blueprints, mutating the shared options dict leaks state across parent registrations.
item.content: Build a fresh per-registration options dict (e.g. via copy) instead of mutating the shared blueprint state, so each parent registration is independent and future registrations aren't affected.

item.title: Propagate parent url_prefix to nested blueprints
item.description: Nested blueprints must inherit the parent's url_prefix when the child has none of its own.
item.content: In the nested registration path, when the child has no url_prefix, explicitly set the child's url_prefix to the parent's state.url_prefix; otherwise the parent prefix is silently dropped.

item.title: Add regression tests for nested blueprint prefixes
item.description: Write a test registering a child under a parent and asserting the combined URL resolves.
item.content: Test that a child blueprint with no prefix, registered under a parent registered with url_prefix='/parent', serves at '/parent/<child-route>'; this fails without the fix and guards against regressions.

item.title: Preserve keyword args when refactoring lambda wrappers
item.description: When changing a lambda that forwards **options to a call, explicitly pass any keyword arguments that were previously absorbed by **options.
item.content: If a function signature gains an explicit parameter (e.g. provide_automatic_options) that was previously passed through **options, update every internal forwarding call (like self.record(lambda s: s.add_url_rule(...))) to pass that parameter explicitly. Otherwise the value silently drops out of the forwarded call.

item.title: Use TypeVar bound to Callable for decorator-preserving wrappers
item.description: Annotate wrapper functions that return the same callable with a TypeVar bound to Callable so type info is preserved.
item.content: Define F = t.TypeVar('F', bound=t.Callable[..., t.Any]) and annotate setupmethod(f: F) -> F, casting the update_wrapper result with t.cast(F, ...). This keeps the decorated function's signature instead of erasing it to plain Callable.

item.title: Fix return annotations revealed by stricter typing
item.description: When tightening typing on a decorator, also correct incorrect return annotations on related methods that the change exposes.
item.content: Changing setupmethod to preserve types surfaced that add_url_rule was annotated -> t.Callable but actually returns None. Audit related signatures (e.g. add_url_rule in both app.py and blueprints.py) and fix them alongside the primary typing change.

item.title: Use request.blueprints instead of custom helper
item.description: When iterating over the current request's blueprint chain, prefer the existing request.blueprints property over a custom helper method.
item.content: Reviewers flagged a custom _request_blueprints() helper and asked why it didn't use request.blueprints. Reuse existing public/established APIs rather than duplicating logic; it reduces surface area and matches reviewer expectations.

item.title: Extract chained calls to variables to avoid wrapping
item.description: When a chained expression wraps awkwardly, assign intermediate results to local variables.
item.content: A reviewer called out weird formatting from a long chain. Pull the inner generator/chain into a named variable (e.g. bp_funcs = chain.from_iterable(...)) so the final line stays readable and within line length.

item.title: Match exception types to semantic intent
item.description: Use ValueError for invalid argument values rather than generic or mismatched exceptions.
item.content: Reviewer said a check 'should be a ValueError'. When validating user-supplied options (like a duplicate or invalid name), raise ValueError with a clear message; also ensure docstrings and CHANGES entries end with periods and follow existing style.

item.title: Use Callable[..., T] for decorator-accepted callables with flexible signatures
item.description: When a decorator registers user functions whose argument signatures vary, annotate with Callable[..., T] rather than a fixed signature.
item.content: Fixed-signature Callables like Callable[[], Any] reject functions that take arguments under mypy. Use Callable[..., T] for template globals/filters/tests so any signature is accepted, and keep the return type accurate (e.g. Callable[..., bool] for tests).

item.title: Match existing changelog style and target the correct release section
item.description: Changelog entries must follow the repo's existing formatting and go under the appropriate version heading.
item.content: Use the same issue-link style as neighboring entries (e.g. ``:issue:`4098```), avoid extra blank lines, keep the description to one concise sentence, and place the entry under the correct version section (e.g. 2.0.2) rather than Unreleased or a future version.

item.title: Don't use code formatting for plain phrases in docs
item.description: Reserve RST code formatting for identifiers and code, not descriptive phrases.
item.content: In changelog and docs, only wrap actual code/identifiers in double backticks; phrases like 'template global' should be plain text. Reviewers flag misuse of code formatting.

item.title: Preserve order when deduplicating a small sequence
item.description: When deduplicating values in a loop, avoid sets because iteration order is not guaranteed and order may matter.
item.content: If order matters, deduplicate with an explicit conditional list (e.g. `[code, None] if code is not None else [None]`) rather than a set literal. Sets are unordered, so `{code, None}` can silently change behavior when the first match wins.

item.title: Deduplicate fallback sentinels in lookup loops
item.description: When a loop iterates over a value plus a fallback like None, guard against the value already being the fallback.
item.content: Patterns like `for c in [code, None]` run the fallback branch twice when `code is None`. Add a conditional so the fallback appears only once, avoiding redundant lookups and duplicate work.

item.title: Keep minimal fixes minimal and explain ordering constraints
item.description: Reviewers may suggest shorter alternatives like set literals; justify why the explicit form is needed.
item.content: When a reviewer proposes a more concise rewrite, check whether it changes semantics (e.g. ordering). If it does, keep the explicit version and briefly note the ordering requirement in the PR description or reply.

item.title: Wrap class-based view handlers with ensure_sync
item.description: To support async handlers in View/MethodView, wrap dispatch calls with current_app.ensure_sync rather than calling them directly.
item.content: In View.as_view's inner view function, call current_app.ensure_sync(self.dispatch_request)(*args, **kwargs). In MethodView.dispatch_request, wrap the resolved method: current_app.ensure_sync(meth)(*args, **kwargs). This lets both sync and async handlers work uniformly.

item.title: Classify async view support as a bug fix
item.description: When a feature was intended in a prior release but missing, reviewers may treat the change as a bug fix, affecting CHANGES.rst wording.
item.content: If the issue references an intended-but-missing capability from an earlier version, frame the CHANGES entry as a fix (e.g., 'Support X with async handlers') rather than a new feature, and avoid unnecessary versionchanged directives.

item.title: Test async support across all view types
item.description: Add async test cases for plain View, MethodView, and blueprint routes to prove the change works end-to-end.
item.content: Define AsyncView (async dispatch_request) and AsyncMethodView (async get/post), register them via add_url_rule with as_view, and parametrize existing async route tests to include those paths. This ensures tests fail without the ensure_sync wrapping.

item.title: Scope doc typo fixes to the exact reported line
item.description: When fixing a documentation typo, change only the specific wording the issue identifies rather than rewriting nearby related lines.
item.content: Reviewers rejected extra edits beyond the reported typo, preferring the original phrasing elsewhere. Keep the diff minimal and targeted to the line the issue names.

item.title: Disambiguate 'method' from 'classmethod' in docs
item.description: When calling something a 'method' in Python docs, clarify it means a regular instance method to avoid confusion with classmethod.
item.content: Phrase it as 'method of the class' or 'corresponding method of a class' so readers don't conflate it with classmethod. Reviewers explicitly requested this clarification.

item.title: Accept reviewer's preferred wording over your own
item.description: When a reviewer suggests alternative phrasing, adopt their exact wording rather than defending the original change.
item.content: The final accepted diff used the reviewer's suggested 'method of the class' phrasing. Incorporate reviewer wording directly to converge faster.

item.title: Match docstring return style to reviewer preference
item.description: When adding :return: docstrings, follow the reviewer's preferred concise phrasing rather than verbose type-prefixed descriptions.
item.content: Reviewers rejected 'bool. ``True`` if able to load config, ``False`` otherwise.' in favor of '``True`` if the file was loaded successfully.' Avoid redundant type prefixes and 'False otherwise' tails; keep return descriptions short and consistent across methods.

item.title: Add blank line before directives in docstrings
item.description: Sphinx/Read the Docs builds require a blank line separating a :return: line from following directives like .. versionadded::.
item.content: When inserting a :return: line into a docstring that already has .. versionadded:: or .. deprecated:: directives, add a blank line between them so the RTD CI build passes.

item.title: Use consistent return wording across similar methods
item.description: Apply the same return description to all sibling methods that share behavior, adjusting only for genuinely different semantics.
item.content: For from_* config loaders, use '``True`` if the file was loaded successfully.' uniformly; for from_mapping which always succeeds, use 'Always returns ``True``.' Keep phrasing parallel so docs read consistently.

item.title: Skip changelog and versionchanged for example/tutorial code
item.description: Reviewers rejected changelog and versionchanged entries for changes to example app code because it is not public API.
item.content: When modifying example applications or tutorial code (e.g. examples/tutorial/), do not add CHANGES.rst entries or `.. versionchanged::` directives. Those are reserved for public API changes; example updates are not useful changelog information.

item.title: Fix check-then-insert races with IntegrityError handling
item.description: Replacing a SELECT-then-INSERT existence check with a try/except around the INSERT commit eliminates the race condition.
item.content: To avoid race conditions in register-style flows, remove the pre-insert existence query and instead wrap the INSERT + commit in try/except catching the database IntegrityError (e.g. db.IntegrityError for sqlite3). Set the validation error in the except branch and redirect in the else branch.

item.title: Update tutorial prose to match refactored code
item.description: The docs tutorial explanation must be rewritten to describe the new try/except flow rather than the removed SELECT check.
item.content: When changing tutorial example code, update the corresponding docs/tutorial/*.rst step-by-step explanation: remove descriptions of deleted queries, describe the new error-handling behavior, and relocate any still-relevant method explanations (like fetchone) to where they are now used.

item.title: Serialize Decimal as string to preserve precision
item.description: When adding JSON support for decimal.Decimal, encode it to str rather than float to avoid precision loss.
item.content: Django and Flask both convert Decimal to str in their JSON encoders. Converting to float loses precision; reviewers explicitly rejected a float-based approach. Use str(o) and expect quoted output like '"0.003"'.

item.title: Test JSON encoders through the public dumps API
item.description: Write tests that call flask.json.dumps directly on the value rather than constructing an encoder manually.
item.content: Reviewers preferred `rv = flask.json.dumps(decimal.Decimal("0.003"))` over manually instantiating the encoder class. This exercises the real code path and keeps tests concise.

item.title: Group new type handling with existing isinstance branches
item.description: Add new serializable types to the existing isinstance check in the JSON default method instead of adding separate branches.
item.content: In Flask's JSONEncoder.default, extend `isinstance(o, uuid.UUID)` to `isinstance(o, (decimal.Decimal, uuid.UUID))` since both convert via str. Also add a CHANGES.rst entry and versionchanged docstrings.

item.title: Store exception objects, not exc_info tuples, for deferred re-raise
item.description: When capturing an exception in a background thread to re-raise later, store the exception instance rather than sys.exc_info().
item.content: sys.exc_info() returns a tuple that cannot be raised directly with `raise exc_info`; you must use `raise exc_info[1].with_traceback(exc_info[2])`. Simpler and safer: capture `except Exception as e: self._exc = e` and later `raise exc`. This preserves the exception type and message for callers.

item.title: Add changelog entries to the correct version section
item.description: Place new CHANGES.rst entries under the unreleased/next patch version, not an already-released version.
item.content: Reviewers reject changelog entries added to a released version. Check the top of CHANGES.rst for the Unreleased or upcoming patch section (e.g., 2.0.2) and add the entry there with the issue reference.

item.title: Write a focused test for deferred exception re-raise
item.description: Test lazy-loading error propagation by constructing the loader with eager loading disabled and directly invoking the flush method.
item.content: Instantiate DispatchingApp with a loader that raises a custom exception and use_eager_loading=False, then assert pytest.raises on the flush method. This isolates the re-raise logic without needing a full CLI invocation.
